Certified type:
- Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" → per schema categories include "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system"... The category here is a non-automatic weighing instrument. I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- Type designations: TLW1XX (X = 0…9). So type is TLW1XX where X varies 0-9. Type designations: ["TLW1XX"]. Hmm, should I list all variants TLW100...TLW199? The cert says "Type : TLW1XX (X = 0…9)". I'll keep "TLW1XX" as the type designation. Possibly note in description that X = 0...9.

Interesting: the cert mentions "Indicator IND360" and "Load cell MTB" — these are the instruments covered in test reports. The certified type is a non-automatic weighing instrument TLW1XX, but the test reports relate to indicator IND360 and load cell MTB. Should these be components? The cert says "The conformity was established by the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated OIML Reports: Indicator IND360: ... Load cell MTB: ..."

So components could include:
- Indicator IND360
- Load cell MTB

These are sub-assemblies named in the cert. I think including them as components is reasonable: role "Indicator", type_designations ["IND360"]; role "Load cell", type_designations ["MTB"].

Recommendation:
- R76-1, edition 2006, scheme A, accuracy classes ["III", "IIII"]. Canonical ID "R76" or "R76-1"? The schema says id canonical e.g. "R60". The cert says "OIML R 76-1:2006". I'll use "R76-1" as the id since that's the specific part. Hmm, canonical... R 76-1 is a part of R76. I'll use "R76-1". Edition: 2006 (int). Accuracy classes: ["(III)", "(IIII)"] or ["III", "IIII"]. I'll use ["III", "IIII"].

Load cell MTB:

- NMi-R60/2000-NL1-05.18C, dated 10 October 2005, 40 pages
- LSfc2015-6001, dated 24 June 2015, 24 pages
- NMi-2641941-01, dated 17 November 2022, 24 pages

Role: type_evaluation_report seems appropriate for these OIML reports. The schema lists roles: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. These are OIML test reports; I'll use "type_evaluation_report" for all.

Revision history:
- revision "0", date 2022-12-08, changes "Initial issue."

Characteristics:
- Accuracy class: (III) or (IIII) → this is type_level. Value as string? The value is two alternatives. I could record as accuracy_class with value "(III) or (IIII)". Or model_level with axis class? It's an alternative, not a matrix. I'll put in type_level: {"value": "(III) or (IIII)", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}. Hmm, but rules say structured values must be object with value/unit. Fine.

- Maximum capacity: Max ≤ 60 kg → value {min: null, max: 60}, unit_symbol "kg"
- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 10 g → value {min: 10, max: null}, unit_symbol "g"
- Maximum number of scale intervals: n ≤ 3000 divisions → value {min: null, max: 3000}, unit_symbol "divisions"? Or unit null with "divisions" as unit_symbol. I'll use unit_symbol "divisions" (not in unitsdb, use raw symbol). Actually "divisions" — raw symbol fine.
- Temperature range: -10 °C / 40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- Power supply voltage: 100 - 240 V AC 50/60 Hz → split:
  - power_supply_voltage: {min:100, max:240}, unit "V"
  - power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60}, unit "Hz"
  - power_supply_type: "AC"
- Software identification Version number: 1.xx.yyyy (y, x = 0…9) → value "1.xx.yyyy" string, maybe note. I'll record software_identification_version with value "1.xx.yyyy".

Model family: Is this a family? Type TLW1XX (X = 0…9) implies many variants TLW100–TLW199. Should I create model_family with models? That would be 100 entries — excessive. The certificate covers a type with wildcard X. I could create model_family with family_name "TLW1XX" and models... hmm. The rule says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. X = 0…9 means two wildcard digits? "TLW1XX (X = 0…9)" — each X can be 0-9, so 100 variants. Creating 100 model entries seems like fabrication/noise. I think it's safer to record the type as "TLW1XX" with a description that X = 0…9, and not enumerate models. Alternatively, create model_family with family_name "TLW1XX" and models as pattern? The schema requires model_id per variant. I'll skip model_family but note in description: "Type TLW1XX (X = 0…9). Certified instrument based on indicator IND360 and load cell MTB."

Actually, the characteristics table applies to the whole weighing instrument. Should the attributes be model_level with variants? No — the table gives single values (Max ≤ 60 kg etc.), not per-model. So type_level.

Components: Indicator IND360 and Load cell MTB. Include as components with roles. The load cell MTB references R60 test reports. Include.

Footnotes: none in this cert.

Matrix tables: none.

Certificate number: "R76/2006-A-NL1-22.22" — full. revision 0 — schema has revision under revision_history as string "0". Certificate-level there's no revision field in schema; number field includes... The number given includes "revision 0" separately. I'll set certificate.number to "R76/2006-A-NL1-22.22". 

oiml_issuer_id: "NL1".

date_issued: "2022-12-08" (8 December 2022, and revision history date 2022-12-08 confirms).

Wait — the load cell report dates: "NMi-R60/2000-NL-02.10A dated 9 April 2002" and "02.10B dated 5 April 2002". Yes as given. "05.18C dated 10 October 2005" — yes, that's what markdown says (even though it looks odd following Nov 4 ones, preserve as given).

For accuracy_class value — maybe better to use "III or IIII"? The original is "(III) or (IIII)". The parentheses are standard class notation. I'll keep "(III) or (IIII)" as string. Actually schema rule says values clean of punctuation like trailing punctuation, but "(III)" is the standard notation. Keep.

For test report roles — should the load cell reports be "test_report" rather than type_evaluation_report? They are OIML test reports for the load cell under R60. Both are test reports associated. I'll keep type_evaluation_report for all; that's consistent.

Should I add model_family given X = 0…9? I decided no. But the schema says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant — it does cover >1 variant conceptually. But enumerating 100 variants is fabricating. I could add model_family with family_name "TLW1XX" and a single models entry? That seems wrong. Alternative: model_family with models list generated TLW100–TLW199? That's mechanical expansion, arguably faithful. But risky and long. I'll omit model_family and describe in description. Actually, maybe include model_family with family_name "TLW1XX" and models with a pattern attribute? models[] requires model_id per variant. Hmm, I could do:

"model_family": {
  "family_name": "TLW1XX",
  "models": [
    {"model_id": "TLW1XX", "label": "X = 0…9", "attributes": {}}
  ]
}

That's a bit redundant. I'll omit it since the cert doesn't enumerate variants. Keep description mention.

Footnote about date of 02.10B: "5 April 2002" — keep.

Ellipsis in description: "X = 0…9" contains the ellipsis character, fine in JSON.

One more: "certificate.number" — should revision be separate? Schema has no revision field at cert level, only revision_history. Fine.
